title: U.S. Coast Guard suspends search for crew of capsized vessel offshore Saipan
description: U.S. Coast Guard Cmdr. Preston Hieb, a search and rescue mission coordinator assigned to Coast Guard Oceania District, describes Coast Guard and partner efforts during the search for the missing crew members of the cargo vessel Mariana April 28, 2026. In total, Coast Guard crews and involved partners searched for over 100 hours, covering over 135,000 square nautical miles. (U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 2nd Class Tyler Robertson)
keywords: Mariana, statement, Suspension, SMC, SAR, search

transcript.text: Good evening . My name is Commander
Preston Hive , and I'm a search and
rescue mission coordinator at Coast
Guard Oceania District . We are deeply
saddened to announce that despite
widespread efforts , we have made the
difficult decision to suspend our
search for the missing crew members of
the Mariana . We offer our heartfelt
condolences to the families of the
Mariana crew , as well as the entire
Saipan community . On April 15th ,
Joint Rescue Coordination Center
Honolulu received a report from the
vessel manager of the Mariana stating
the vessel's starboard engine was
disabled with six people on board .
Coast Guard watch standards established
a one hour communication schedule with
the Mariana , but lost communications
with the vessel later that same evening .
Watchander coordinated the launch of a
C-130 Hercules airplane from Coast
Guard Air Station Barbars Point and the
crew of our Coast Guard cutter
Frederick Hatch , to search for the
missing vessel and crew members . Coast
Guard cutter Oliver Henry later joined
the search as well . On the morning of
April 17th , a US Coast Guard airplane
sighted an overturned vessel
approximately 34 nautical miles
northeast of Pagan . On April 19th ,
the US Air Force's 31st rescue Squadron
arrived on scene with the overturned
vessel and deployed para rescue men ,
divers , and boats . We were able to
confirm the identity of the vessel as
the cargo ship Mariana . On April 20th ,
US Air Force's 31st rescue squadron
divers recovered one deceased
individual from the overturned Mariana .
The five remaining crew members are
still missing . Alongside US military
and international partners , the US
Coast Guard searched more than 100
hours , covering over 135,000 square
nautical miles , an area larger than
the state of California . Search
efforts included aerial searches of the
Northern Mariana Islands for any signs
of survivors on land .
We are grateful for the efforts of our
partners , including the US Air Force ,
US Navy , Japan Coast Guard , and the
Royal New Zealand Air Force . The
decision to suspend a search is an
incredibly difficult one that is only
made after very careful consideration
of all available information . From
working and communicating with the
families , I know how devastated they
are by this outcome . I have also
witnessed the incredible resilience and
compassion of the entire Saipan
community . The Coast Guard offers
deepest condolences to the families and
friends of the Mariana crew as they
continue to process and heal . Thank
you for your time .
